current_example.problem:
Which of the following equalities are true given that
$D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1 \big\}.$

I. $\displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} e^{\sqrt{xy}} \,\text{d}A  = \int_{0}^{1}  \int_{0}^{2}e^{\sqrt{xy}}\,  \text{d}y \, \text{d}x$

II. $\displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} e^{\sqrt{xy}}\,\text{d}A  = \int_{0}^{2}  \int_{0}^{1} e^{\sqrt{xy}}\, \text{d}y\,  \text{d}x$

III. $\displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} e^{\sqrt{xy}} \,\text{d}A = \int_{0}^{1}  \int_{0}^{2}e^{\sqrt{xy}}\,  \text{d}x \, \text{d}y$
current_example.worked_solution:
We notice that: 

- the limits for the variable $x$ are from ${\color{blue}0}$ to ${\color{blue}2}$, and

- the limits for the variable $y$ are from ${\color{red}0}$ to ${\color{red}1}.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{e}^{\sqrt{xy}}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{\sqrt{xy}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the region of integration is rectangular, we can simply swap the order of integration. This gives

$$
\iint\limits_{D} e^{\sqrt{xy}} \,\text{d}A  
= \int_{\color{blue}0}^{\color{blue}{2}} \left[ \int_{\color{red}0}^{\color{red}1} e^{\sqrt{xy}}\,\text{d}{\color{red}y} \right] \text{d}{\color{blue}x} .
$$

So, the correct answer is "II and III only".
